title: View-transition list reorder
description: Animates items moving to their new positions when a list is sorted, filtered, or reordered, using the View Transitions API with per-item view-transition-name, so users can track where an item went. Falls back to an instant update without the API or under reduced motion.
intent: Help users follow items through a sort or reorder instead of losing their place when the list jumps.
characteristics: each item gets a stable, unique view-transition-name
feature-detect document.startViewTransition and update instantly otherwise
reduced motion: skip the transition, keep the state change
keyboard focus stays on the same item after reorder
interaction: Triggered by sort, filter, or drag-and-drop reorder; during the transition the page remains interactive after it finishes (keep it short); rapid repeated sorts skip to the final state.
responsive: Identical behavior across sizes; cap the number of named elements on long lists (only visible items) to keep it smooth on low-end devices.
accessibility: Announce the new order or sort state in text (aria-sort or a live region); focus does not move unexpectedly; respects prefers-reduced-motion.
limitations: Same-document View Transitions are not supported in every browser; treat as progressive enhancement.
Hundreds of named elements in one transition degrade performance.
